name: Longest Edge Bisection (LEB) Tetrahedral Hierarchy
definition: A hierarchical subdivision scheme for tetrahedra starting from a cubic domain split into six initial tetrahedra. It ensures element quality does not degrade because recursively splitting a tetrahedron three times yields smaller tetrahedra with exactly the same shape and quality as the initial one, resulting in only well-shaped tetrahedra.
summary: Longest Edge Bisection Tetrahedral Hierarchy generates adaptive, crack-free conforming meshes by splitting tetrahedra along their longest edge, eliminating the need for complex stitching required by octrees.
